newsitem.title: CANADA: Teleglobe unit working on first partnership.
newsitem.headline: Teleglobe unit working on first partnership.

text.p: Teleglobe Inc's new media unit will celebrate its first anniversary with a brand-new partnership, its president and chief operating officer Pierre Laferriere said on Wednesday.
But details of the union which the company is working on and what will emerge from it were scarce "for competitive reasons."
He said the tripartite union will include a large Canadian telephone carrier and a small entrepreneurial company in an industry he declined to identify.
"It would be too obvious," Laferriere told Reuters after a presentation at the Canadian Business Telecommunications Alliance Telecon conference.

Laferriere said in the year since the inception of the new media unit, it has considered about 40 partnership ideas and settled first on this one. He expects to be able to give details of the deal in the first half of 1997.
In his presentation, Laferrieree put Teleglobe's new media unit -- still very much in its infancy -- in the context of the emerging market of new media.
He dismissed last year's notion that the telecommunications and media industries would ultimately converge into one super-information industry.
"Up until a year or so ago, we were under the impression that these two industries were going to merge," Laferriere said.
"It isn't the way we see it...What we are seeing is that in between the two is an entirely new industry that's emerging that has still very ill-defined boundaries," he added.

New media, the narrowly targeted delivery of information to a selective audience where, when and how that audience wants it most often via the internet, takes advantage of discontinuities, or changes in the traditional way a given industry conducts itself.

Teleglobe new media is looking at ideas such as Physicians' On-line, an internet service for doctors, Amazon Books, an on-line book order warehouse which is vastly successful, and Wit Capital, the world's first on-line brokerage and merchant bank as examples of clever products.

Laferriere said the most likely new media business to succeed is one that fits into a clear market niche, a vision of a new service or a new way of delivering an old one, one that is backed by a commited entrepreneur, one that has barriers to entry by competitors, and one based on open computer architecture.
The entrepreneur, according to Laferriere, is the most important ingredient in the mix. He said that Microsoft Corp is the first company in history to try and catch two technology waves.
"It isn't obvious they're going to succeed in a second wave. This new industry belongs to entrepreneurs," Laferriere said.
He said that Teleglobe would consider deals with large carriers but an entrepreneurial company must always be part of the mix to lend vision and a nimbleness of thought.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
